growth_thesis.basis: Royalty figures and the licensing dependence are stated in the 10-K and 10-Q. The link to continued growth is inferred.
growth_thesis.claim: Growth in Magic depends on third-party licenses. Universes Beyond sets use partner brands such as Final Fantasy, Avatar and Spider-Man, and Hasbro pays royalties on them. Q3 royalties rose to $142.1 million from $114.3 million. For growth to continue, key licenses must be renewed or replaced on acceptable terms.
quotes: A significant part of our strategy for our consumer products business and our Wizards and Digital Gaming business is to license premium and well-recognized intellectual property for the development of products.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in the 10-Q MD&A. The dependence on future content slates is inferred from the comparison to the prior year.
growth_thesis.claim: Consumer Products grew modestly in Q3 on entertainment-linked licensed brands. Marvel toy and game sales rose $46.8 million and the new KPop Demon Hunters license added $13.3 million. Continued growth requires a steady slate of third-party content releases.
quotes: an increase in toy and game sales for Marvel of $46.8 million as a result of a strong content slate

growth_thesis.basis: The announcement is stated in the 10-Q. Its effect on growth is inferred, and no financial terms are given.
growth_thesis.claim: A new licensed franchise is announced for 2027. Hasbro is to become global primary toy licensee for Harry Potter, and it also announced collaborations on Voltron and Street Fighter. This can only support growth if those properties launch and consumers accept the products.
quotes: The announcement of a multi-year licensing partnership starting in 2027 with Warner Bros. Discovery Global Consumer Products

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in the 10-Q MD&A, which also cites a roughly $10.1 million decrease in recurring tariff expense. The one-off nature is inferred.
growth_thesis.claim: Q3 profit growth was helped by lower cost of sales and by tariff refunds, which should not be treated as a repeatable source of growth. Cost of sales fell to 24.1% of net revenues from 29.9%, with $54.5 million of IEEPA refunds recorded as a cost reduction. The 10-Q says the company expects to receive the remaining $13.0 million of Phase 2 and Phase 3 refunds.
quotes: The Company expects to receive the remaining $13.0 million of Phase 2 and Phase 3 IEEPA tariff refunds within the next six months.

growth_thesis.basis: The savings figures are stated in the 10-K. Their contribution to Q3 2026 is inferred from the release's reference to cost productivity.
growth_thesis.claim: Cost savings under the Operational Excellence programme are a margin driver. The 10-K says almost $800 million of gross savings were delivered through 2025, toward a $1.0 billion commitment. Margin gains can continue only if the remaining savings are realised and not offset by lower sales or higher expenses.
quotes: Through 2025, we have delivered almost $800 million of gross cost savings and are well on our path to our previous $1.0 billion commitment.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in the release and 10-Q. The dependence on partners is inferred.
growth_thesis.claim: Digital and licensed gaming and licensing are smaller contributors, and the evidence is mixed. Q3 digital and licensed gaming grew 3%, and Monopoly Go! contributed $41 million in Q3 and $127 million year to date. Licensing revenue fell to $144.3 million from $152.6 million in Q3. Continued contribution depends on partner games such as Monopoly Go! sustaining performance.
quotes: Digital and licensed gaming grew 3%.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in the 10-Q statements. The link to growth capacity is inferred.
growth_thesis.claim: Cash generation supports reinvestment and shareholder returns alongside growth. Nine-month operating cash flow was $907.3 (table in millions) against $490.0 (table in millions). Financing outflows included dividends of $296.1 (table in millions) and repurchases of $149.3 (table in millions). This continues only if earnings stay high and working capital needs stay contained.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in the Q3 earnings release. Whether it will be met is not shown.
growth_thesis.claim: Management raised its 2026 outlook, which implies it expects the growth drivers to persist through year-end. It now expects revenue up 7-9% in constant currency and an adjusted operating margin of 27-28%. This requires the Magic lineup and licensed content to deliver as management expects.
quotes: Adjusted operating margin of 27-28% (previously 25-26%)

material_events.basis: stated in P4; the cash flow statement F3 shows the same amount as impairment of capitalized software, and P6 repeats it as an impairment related to digital games.
material_events.claim: Hasbro recorded a one-time non-cash impairment of $56.4 million after deciding to refocus its Digital Games portfolio.
quotes: a one-time $56.4 million non-cash impairment charge in the second quarter of 2026 related to the Company's decision to refocus the Digital Games portfolio

material_events.basis: stated in the 10-K MD&A (P3); the 10-Q income statement F2 shows the same charge in the prior-year nine months.
material_events.claim: Hasbro recorded a non-cash goodwill impairment of $1,021.9 million in the Consumer Products segment, triggered by tariffs and macroeconomic headwinds. It did not recur in 2026.
quotes: During 2025, the Company recorded a $1,021.9 million non-cash goodwill impairment charge associated with goodwill assigned to reporting units within the Company's Consumer Products segment.

material_events.basis: stated in the 10-Q MD&A (P4) and the 10-Q risk factors (P5).
material_events.claim: Hasbro identified unauthorized access to its network. Order processing, shipping and invoicing were disrupted, which hurt net sales and operating profit in the second quarter, especially in Consumer Products. The company says systems are restored and third-quarter operations were normal.
quotes: In late March 2026, the Company identified unauthorized access to our network.

The impacts of these system disruptions included order processing, shipping, and invoicing delays, resulting in a negative impact on net sales and operating profit during the second quarter, particularly within the Consumer Products segment.

material_events.basis: stated in the 10-Q MD&A (P4); P6 reports approximately the same tariff refund benefit.
material_events.claim: Hasbro recorded $54.5 million of IEEPA tariff recoveries as a reduction to Cost of sales. Part was received in cash and the rest is a receivable.
quotes: Hasbro recorded a total of $54.5 million of tariff recoveries as a reduction to Cost of sales within the Consolidated Statements of Operations

material_events.basis: stated in the 8-K earnings release headline (P6).
material_events.claim: In its third-quarter earnings release, Hasbro raised its full-year outlook and doubled its share repurchase target.
quotes: Raises 2026 Financial Outlook & Doubles Share Repurchase Target

material_events.basis: stated in the 10-Q MD&A Recent Developments (P4); the announcement date is not given.
material_events.claim: Hasbro announced a multi-year licensing partnership with Warner Bros. Discovery Global Consumer Products, making it the global primary toy licensee for the world of Harry Potter. The partnership starts in a future year.
quotes: The announcement of a multi-year licensing partnership starting in 2027 with Warner Bros. Discovery Global Consumer Products, making Hasbro the global primary toy licensee for the world of Harry Potter and the upcoming HBO Original Harry Potter series.

risks.basis: stated in the filings: the concentration and risk language is explicit; the revenue shares are read from the cited tables.
risks.claim: Profit and sales are concentrated in Magic: The Gathering. Its third-quarter revenue was 616.1 of 1,595.3 total net revenues (table in millions), and Wizards and Digital Gaming operating profit was 367.4 against 173.8 for Consumer Products. The company itself flags increasing concentration of sales and profits in Magic.
quotes: particularly for brands such as Magic: The Gathering in which we have seen an increasing concentration of our sales and profits;

Because our strategy emphasizes growing a focused set of franchises and expanding our higher-margin games and digital businesses, including MAGIC: THE GATHERING and DUNGEONS & DRAGONS, adverse trends affecting consumer demand for, or engagement with, any of these key brands could disproportionately impact our results of operations.

risks.basis: stated in the 10-Q MD&A and the earnings release risk factors.
risks.claim: Third-quarter cost of sales and operating profit include $54.5 million of IEEPA tariff refunds, a benefit that may not repeat. $13.0 million of that is still receivable, and the company warns refunds could be delayed, reduced or not received.
quotes: The Company expects to receive the remaining $13.0 million of Phase 2 and Phase 3 IEEPA tariff refunds within the next six months.
the risk that refunds we have recognized or expect to receive are delayed, reduced or not received;

risks.basis: inferred from balance sheet figures and the release's prefunding statement; no covenant or maturity schedule is in the packet.
risks.claim: The current portion of long-term debt was 893.9 at quarter-end (table in millions), against cash and cash equivalents of 850.7 and short-term investments of 576.2. Near-term maturities are material relative to cash on hand, and shareholder equity is thin relative to liabilities.
quotes: During the quarter, the Company deployed $79 million toward debt reduction through open-market bond repurchases and U.S. Treasury purchases to prefund the 2026 and 2027 bond maturities.

risks.basis: stated in the 10-Q MD&A and risk factors.
risks.claim: The unauthorized network access identified in late March disrupted order processing, shipping and invoicing in the second quarter and cost about $1.0 million in the third quarter and $11.8 million over nine months. No insurance proceeds had been recognized, and further incidents or costs, including legal proceedings, remain possible.
quotes: The Company did not recognize any insurance proceeds during the three and nine months ended September 27, 2026 related to the unauthorized network access.

Any further incidents of unauthorized access could result in adverse effects on our business, operations, financial results, and financial reporting; and any further impacts related to the unauthorized access or other similar unauthorized activity may result in increased costs, including from any legal proceedings.

risks.basis: stated in the filings; the link between the impairment and future write-offs is inferred from the risk factor language.
risks.claim: The digital games strategy carries write-off risk. The company recorded a $56.4 million non-cash impairment when it refocused the Digital Games portfolio, and it kept capitalizing software development spend of 77.8 over nine months (table in millions).
quotes: partially offset by a one-time $56.4 million non-cash impairment charge in the second quarter of 2026 related to the Company's decision to refocus the Digital Games portfolio.
we face the risk of significant write-offs

risks.basis: stated in the 10-Q MD&A; materiality is inferred from the size of the figures.
risks.claim: Parts of the portfolio outside Magic are weakening. Licensing revenue fell to 144.3 from 152.6 in the third quarter (table in millions), and Reinvent Brands net revenues fell 15.8%, led by Nerf, Furby and Nanomals.
quotes: The change was primarily driven by lower consumer products licensing revenue, particularly related to Peppa Pig and Nerf, partially offset by growth in Transformers.
